verification_rule: A component reaches TESTED only after an INDEPENDENT re-run by the supervising agent, never on a builder's self-report. Hermes claimed a completed delegation on 2026-08-16 that the bridge log and the filesystem both disproved; that is why this rule exists.
note_on_states: TESTED means proven on this machine against mocks. DEPLOYED means it exists as a running cloud resource. VERIFIED means observed working against the real thing, with the observation captured under evidence/. Every resource declared in infra/main.bicep is now VERIFIED. README.md is authoritative over this file.

oidc_federation.notes: EXERCISED, FAILED TWICE, NOW WORKING. (1) AADSTS700213 - the deploy job is environment-gated, so GitHub presents ...:environment:production, not ...:ref:refs/heads/main. (2) AADSTS700213 again - this account's GitHub default subject is ID-QUALIFIED: repo:Alhamwis@<ownerId>/OpsBridge365@<repoId>:environment:production. use_default was already true, so it cannot be normalised; Entra must match the ID-qualified string. That form is rename-proof, which is a security improvement, not a workaround. The app holds exactly ONE federated credential

graph_admin_consent.notes: Exactly three admin-consented APPLICATION permissions: User.Read.All, Device.Read.All, Sites.Selected. Zero delegated grants. Granted PROGRAMMATICALLY via appRoleAssignments, not a portal click, then verified by reading the consent state back

key_vault.notes: RBAC-enabled, soft-delete on, standard SKU. The secret graph-client-secret is stored as a Key Vault REFERENCE on both workloads - keyVaultUrl set, no inline value - and reaches the container as a secretRef. Deployment outputs are exactly apiFqdn, identityPrincipalId, jobName, keyVaultName, logAnalyticsWorkspaceId: no secret. The vault denies the HUMAN OPERATOR with ForbiddenByRbac; only the managed identity holds Key Vault Secrets User

corrections_made_during_build: Hermes reported a completed Claude Code delegation that never happened - no DELEGATE entry in the bridge log, no files on disk. Engineering was moved to a direct bridge call; Hermes was kept for verification only.
One app registration was being used for BOTH the OIDC deploy login and the Graph runtime identity, so a leaked Graph secret would have carried Azure rights. Split into two.

Docs specified the Intune scope DeviceManagementManagedDevices.Read.All, but the code calls GET /devices, which needs Device.Read.All. Consent would have succeeded and the app would have failed at runtime with 403.
/healthz called get_settings() and returned 503 without credentials, so Docker's HEALTHCHECK would have killed every unconfigured container.
verify-opsbridge.ps1 reported 'az not installed' when az was installed - a User PATH change does not reach an already-running process tree.
Secret scanning was a stated requirement and was absent from CI; a history-scanning gitleaks gate was added.

An integration test asserted 403 on an UNGRANTED site's metadata and failed against a correctly-configured tenant. Sites.Selected does not hide a site's existence; it withholds data and refuses enumeration. The security property was real, the assertion was aimed at the wrong surface.

The federated credential was created for ref:refs/heads/main, but the deploy job is environment-gated and therefore presents environment:production. Deploy failed with AADSTS700213 after three green jobs.

The corrected subject STILL failed with AADSTS700213, because this account's GitHub default subject is ID-qualified with owner and repo numeric ids. use_default was already true, so there was nothing to normalise - Entra had to match the ID-qualified string. Kept rather than worked around: that form is rename-proof.

The resource group was created in eastus, which the subscription's allowed-regions policy forbids (RequestDisallowedByAzure). Recreated in westus2. main.bicep needed no change because it takes location from resourceGroup().location.

Five resource providers were unregistered on the fresh subscription (MissingSubscriptionRegistration), and ARM names one per failure, so this arrived as a sequence rather than one error. All registered.

THE MOST VALUABLE ONE: the Log Analytics failure alert would not have fired. It matched config_error; app/sync.py's other failure status is graph_error, and the deliberately-triggered failure emitted that one. The query returned 0 hits against a genuinely Failed job. It was syntactically valid, pointed at the right workspace, and matched a status the app really emits - inspection would never have caught it. Corrected to cover both statuses plus Traceback/CRITICAL; returns 2 hits against the same failure. An untested alert is an assumption, not a control.

Sites.Selected with role 'write' cannot create SharePoint lists - previously stated as an untested expectation. Resolved by a throwaway bootstrap app holding Sites.FullControl.All for the schema creation only, which was then deleted, rather than by widening the runtime identity.
